message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering newly reported or updated public vulnerability information from the last 24 hours. Relevant findings were confirmed for SonicWall, FortiOS/Fortinet, Microsoft Windows/Office/SQL Server/Defender families, Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Adobe Creative Cloud, RabbitMQ, Ubuntu, and Apache Tomcat on Ubuntu.

**Finding 1: SonicWall SMA 1000 Series multiple vulnerabilities**

- Product: SonicWall / Dell SonicWall SMA 1000 Series
- Issue: CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410 / SNWLID-2026-0008
- Severity: Critical for CVE-2026-15409 (CVSS 10.0); High for CVE-2026-15410 (CVSS 7.2)
- Description: SonicWall reports server-side request forgery and remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting SMA 1000 Series 12.4.3 and 12.5.0 firmware branches. SonicWall states these vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes SonicWall and Dell SonicWall, and SMA 1000 is a SonicWall secure access product.
- Source: SonicWall product notice, published and updated July 14, 2026: https://www.sonicwall.com/support/notices/product-notice-sma-1000-series-affected-by-multiple-vulnerabilities/kA1VN000001nv6D0AQ

**Finding 2: Fortinet FortiOS path traversal vulnerability**

- Product: Fortigate/FortiOS
- Issue: CVE-2026-59839 / Fortinet FG-IR-26-151
- Severity: Medium, CVSS 5.5 from Fortinet CNA data in NVD
- Description: NVD lists a Fortinet path traversal issue affecting multiple FortiOS branches, with possible unauthorized code or command execution according to the CVE description.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Fortigate/FortiOS, and the CVE explicitly names FortiOS versions as affected.
- Source: NVD CVE-2026-59839, published July 14 and modified July 15, 2026: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-59839

**Finding 3: Microsoft July 2026 security update batch**

- Product: Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Office, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft Defender, and related Microsoft components
- Issue: July 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, including CVE-2026-56155 and many critical RCE vulnerabilities
- Severity: Mixed; Cisco Talos reports 57 Microsoft-rated Critical vulnerabilities and two exploited-in-the-wild vulnerabilities
- Description: Microsoft released a large July security update set. Cisco Talos reports 622 vulnerabilities overall, including critical RCE issues in Windows services, Office, SQL Server, Defender, and other monitored Microsoft families.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 10, Microsoft Office, Microsoft Edge, MSSQL, Microsoft .NET, PowerShell, Windows Defender, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, TFS / Azure DevOps, and Azure AD Connect.
- Source: Cisco Talos Microsoft Patch Tuesday review, July 14, 2026: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/microsoft-patch-tuesday-july-2026/

**Finding 4: Google Chrome Stable Channel security update**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: Chrome 150.0.7871.124/.125 security update, including CVE-2026-15764, CVE-2026-15765, CVE-2026-15766, CVE-2026-15767, and additional fixes
- Severity: Includes Critical and High issues as stated by Google
- Description: Google released Chrome Stable updates for Windows, Mac, and Linux on July 14 with 15 security fixes, including critical use-after-free flaws and high-severity memory-safety issues.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Google Chrome.
- Source: Google Chrome Releases, July 14, 2026: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/07/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_0353146366.html

**Finding 5: Mozilla Firefox 152.0.6 security update**

- Product: Mozilla Firefox
- Issue: MFSA 2026-67 / CVE-2026-15718 and CVE-2026-15719
- Severity: Critical
- Description: Mozilla announced Firefox 152.0.6 on July 14 to fix two critical vulnerabilities. Mozilla says exploit code is public for both issues, but it is not aware of attacks in the wild abusing them.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Mozilla Firefox.
- Source: Mozilla MFSA 2026-67: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-67/

**Finding 6: Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop Application security update**

- Product: Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop Application
- Issue: APSB26-77 / CVE-2026-48272 and CVE-2026-48344
- Severity: Critical, CVSS 7.8
- Description: Adobe released a Windows Creative Cloud Desktop update fixing two critical privilege-escalation vulnerabilities. Adobe states it is not aware of exploitation in the wild for these issues.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Adobe Creative Cloud.
- Source: Adobe APSB26-77, published July 14, 2026: https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/creative-cloud/apsb26-77.html

**Finding 7: RabbitMQ management UI vulnerability**

- Product: RabbitMQ
- Issue: CVE-2026-57211 / GHSA-7v84-m3g5-vxq6
- Severity: Medium by GitHub CNA score (6.5); NVD also shows a Critical enrichment score, so severity should be reviewed against local deployment conditions
- Description: RabbitMQ on Windows can make outbound DNS and SMB requests to attacker-controlled UNC paths through the management UI static file handler when multiple management extension plugins are enabled.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes RabbitMQ, and the source explicitly names RabbitMQ server.
- Source: OSV CVE-2026-57211, modified July 15, 2026: https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2026-57211

**Finding 8: Ubuntu security notices**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: Multiple Ubuntu Security Notices published July 15, including USN-8552-1 Sympa, USN-8551-1 Tomcat, USN-8550-1 libslirp, USN-8549-1 idna, USN-8548-1 Linux kernel, USN-8547-1 Linux kernel, and USN-8545-1 Linux kernel HWE
- Severity: Varies by notice; the listing does not provide a single severity for the batch
- Description: Canonical published several Ubuntu notices fixing vulnerabilities across maintained Ubuntu releases, including server-relevant packages and kernel updates.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu, and one of the notices also overlaps with Apache Tomcat in Products.txt.
- Source: Ubuntu Security Notices listing: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Possible matches needing review**

**Microsoft Edge Chromium fixes**

- Microsoft Edge is in Products.txt. Microsoft’s Edge security release notes for July 14 say Microsoft is aware of recent Chromium security fixes and is actively working on a security fix. Because that wording does not confirm an Edge release was available in the checked window, I did not count it as a confirmed patched Edge finding.
- Source: Microsoft Edge security release notes: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for SonicWall SMA 1000 because SonicWall confirms active exploitation. Microsoft July updates should also be prioritized because Microsoft/Talos report exploited vulnerabilities and many Microsoft-rated Critical issues across monitored product families. Browser and desktop findings should move through normal accelerated patch channels due to critical Chrome, Firefox, and Adobe Creative Cloud fixes.
